root_cause.text: `btrfs_quota_enable()` in Btrfs qgroup enablement mishandled the `btrfs_search_slot_for_read()` return value `> 0` by continuing to reuse `path` after the search had reached the end of the tree, leading to invalid leaf/path access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explains that when `btrfs_search_slot_for_read()` returns `1`, “we have reached the end of the tree and therefore the path is not valid,” yet the old code did `continue;` in `fs/btrfs/qgroup.c`; the fix changes this to `break;` to stop accessing the invalid path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop the quota-enable tree scan when the search reaches the end of the tree instead of continuing the loop.
intent_record.what: In btrfs_quota_enable(), the handling of a positive return value from the tree search was changed: the code previously used `continue;` and now uses `break;`, and the surrounding comment was rewritten to explain that this case means the end of the tree has been reached rather than a condition to skip to the next iteration.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if the search unexpectedly returns a positive value, the loop will now terminate instead of repeatedly continuing the scan. This prevents the function from unnecessarily looping when there are no more matching items/leaves to process, and aligns the control flow with reaching the end of the tree.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this snippet. The fix is explicitly added: after handling a root item, the code now does `btrfs_release_path(path);` before calling `add_qgroup_item(...)`, which prevents reusing a held tree_root path while accessing quota_root. It also re-looks up the root item with `ret = btrfs_search_slot_for_read(tree_root, &found_key, path, 1, 0);` and handles `ret > 0` safely with `continue;`, so there is no reuse of an invalid path after an end-of-tree condition. The old buggy behavior of continuing to use `path` after a positive return from `btrfs_search_slot_for_read()` is not shown here.
